leukemia.plain: A cancer of the blood. The body makes too many unhealthy white blood cells.

bone marrow.plain: The soft middle of bones where blood cells are made.

induction.plain: The first phase of chemo. It aims to clear the leukemia from the blood.

port.plain: A small device under the skin, linked to a vein, so medicine and blood tests do not need a new needle each time.

counts.plain: Blood counts. They show how many infection-fighting and other cells are in the blood. Chemo can lower them.

mercaptopurine.plain: A chemo medicine taken as a pill by mouth.

chemo.plain: Strong medicine that kills fast-growing cells, including cancer cells.

child life.plain: A specialist who uses play and pictures to help children understand and cope with hospital care.
